requirement: Make heating decisions from a sensor's temperature property with a dead band, and build fake sensors whose property returns scripted readings that tests can count.
skeleton: Sensor protocol with a celsius property, fake_sensor attaching a PropertyMock with list side_effect to type of a MagicMock, decide validating band and branching on one reading, and average summing several reads.
caption: Property reads scripted with unittest.mock.PropertyMock. Sensor is a typing.Protocol whose celsius is a read-only property. fake_sensor(*readings) raises ValueError saying it needs at least one reading, otherwise creates a MagicMock and a PropertyMock whose side_effect is the list of readings, and attaches the PropertyMock to type(sensor), because properties live on the class and every MagicMock instance has its own class, so each fake keeps its own readings. It returns the sensor and the PropertyMock so tests can count reads. decide(sensor, target, band=0.5) raises ValueError saying band must be positive before reading anything, then reads celsius exactly once and returns heat below target minus band, cool above target plus band and idle inside the band, edges included. average(sensor, samples) raises ValueError when samples is below 1 and otherwise returns the mean of that many consecutive reads. The fixture asserts that with target 20 the readings 19.4, 19.5, 20.0, 20.5 and 20.6 give heat, idle, idle, idle and cool, that decide calls the property once even when a second reading is scripted, that average of 19, 20 and 24 is 21 with call_count 3, that band 0 raises ValueError without a read, that zero samples raises ValueError, that two fakes return their own readings, and that an empty fake_sensor raises ValueError.

plan.intent: Test code that reads a changing property
constraints: The property is read once per decision
The band edges are idle, outside is heat or cool
band at or below zero raises ValueError before any read
Each fake sensor has its own scripted readings

rationale.teaches: Attach PropertyMock to type(mock) and assert on the PropertyMock itself to control and count property reads.
rationale.why: Assigning a PropertyMock to the instance just stores the mock object, and reading a live property twice lets two different values drive one decision.

ops.docstring: Script property reads with a PropertyMock attached to the mock's own type.

ops.source:
def fake_sensor(*readings: float) -> tuple[MagicMock, PropertyMock]:
    """A sensor whose celsius property returns readings in order, and that property."""
    if not readings:
        raise ValueError("fake_sensor needs at least one reading")
    sensor = MagicMock()
    prop = PropertyMock(side_effect=list(readings))
    type(sensor).celsius = prop
    return sensor, prop

candidates.why_wrong: Setting the PropertyMock on the instance returns the mock object instead of readings.
A reading exactly on the lower edge heats instead of staying idle.
The property is read twice, so two different readings drive one decision.
A zero band is accepted and the sensor is read anyway.
The default dead band is 1.0 instead of 0.5 degrees.
